sermon.title: Why I Go to Church
sermon.speaker: Church members (multiple unnamed speakers)
sermon.summary: Three church members share why they go to church. One urges obeying God’s command not to forsake assembling, citing Psalm 84 and Psalm 92. Another describes finding koinonia—deep brotherly love—that carried her through hard times. A former police lieutenant compares church to a training camp, where believers learn and grow to fight evil.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Psalm 84:4 heard as “84 forces”; recording starts mid-sentence. Sensitive content kept as spoken: a sister who “deserved to be kicked out” of church; a pastor preaching only for pay called a hypocrite; a DOA investigation with cockroach bites on a body; mention of witnessing to Muslims.

chunks.section_question: What does the church do for believers?
chunks.short_answer: It stirs up love, bonds us together and makes us one team. God’s commandment says not to forsake assembling together as we see the day approaching.
